question: A store announces two successive discounts of 30% and 25%. What is the final sale price (in ₹) of a shirt costing ₹1,200?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

By successive method

Final SP = 1200 × (70)/(100) × (75)/(100) = ₹630

∴ The final sale price of the shirt is ₹630.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

A store announces two successive discounts of 30% and 25%

Concept used:

Effective discount of two successive discounts = (A + B - {AB over 100})\%

SP = MP × (100-Discount)/(100)

Calculation:

Final discount% = 30 + 25 - (30 × 25)/100 = 47.5%

Final SP of the shirt = 1200 × (100-47.5)/(100) = 1200 × (52.5)/(100) = ₹630

**∴ The final sale price of the shirt is ₹630.**
